chapter: Working with Duke and final reflections
title: Advice to young people: take advantage of opportunities
summary: Whaley credits his mother for making him study and recalls starving eight months in New York.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Well, to the future generations, long after you and I are gone, they're gonna hear these tapes and know about you and I've taken some pictures of you, so on some of these tapes you can hear some clicks and things, so that they will know what you look like and can hear your voice.
What do you want to say to them, to give them any kind of advice about your times, Tom.
Well, see, I had a very good mother, and she kept us in line, she made us study and take advantage of your opportunities. If you don't take advantage of your opportunities, you'll never get nowhere.
Now I came out here -- in New York, I didn't know nobody, but I met a whole lot of people, see, and

I left Sweatman for a guy I never met, but I knew him from Boston, see, and he had a band he wanted me to join, so I went with him -- and I didn't stay with him but a week, and then I came back and I starved for eight months.
I owed the landlady eight months rent here, but I told her I'll pay her, I'll get the money.
Well, that's beautiful. But what advice do you have for these young people know about music -- what future do you see through music?
